issue.title: Bug: SONiC Build uses `sudo rm -rf` as build user

failure.body:
### Is it platform specific

generic

### Importance or Severity

High

### Description of the bug

During the SONiC build process, part of the build is doing a `sudo rm -rf` of a directory which is both dangerous to do and not a given that users will be able to do: https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-buildimage/blob/master/Makefile.work#L305. @jusherma left a comment on the PR to this effect: https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-buildimage/pull/27574#discussion_r3517821383

### Steps to Reproduce

Run any SONiC build target and it will attempt sudo access. If your user doesn't have passwordless sudo access it will sit _forever_ until user intervention to either enter password or enter incorrect 3 times (and this will happen on multiple versions so for example will happen on BOTH stages for bookworm and trixie).

### Actual Behavior and Expected Behavior

SONiC should not assume sudo access for builds both from a security/safety perspective and as Justin mentioned a build repro view, rather, in a case where root level permissions are "required" to delete (like is needed for fsroot) it should be done through docker to remove this dependency.

### Relevant log output

```shell
grboudre@<server>:sonic-buildimage$ time make TRUSTED_GPG_URLS='' SMARTSWITCH=1 INCLUDE_DHCP_SERVER=y all
+++ --- Making all --- +++
./scripts/run_with_retry make EXTRA_DOCKER_TARGETS=all BLDENV=bookworm -f Makefile.work bookworm
make[1]: Entering directory '/nobackup/grboudre/202605-cpn/sonic-buildimage'
WARNING: bridge-nf-call-iptables is disabled
WARNING: bridge-nf-call-ip6tables is disabled
This is your AD password:

resolution.title: [build]: Avoid host sudo for Docker root cleanup
resolution.description:
This reverts the change of `Makefile.work` from commit 8d9637d2fa4638f76e86267026c43c57525cfb54.

#### Why I did it
Fix https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-buildimage/issues/28692
The host-side `sudo rm -rf` cleanup requires passwordless sudo and can block a build waiting for a password. Root-owned Docker data should instead be removed through Docker without requiring elevated privileges on the build host.
##### Work item tracking
- Microsoft ADO **(number only)**:

#### How I did it
Reverted the change of `Makefile.work` from commit 8d9637d2fa4638f76e86267026c43c57525cfb54. Replaced the host-side `sudo rm -rf` command with a short-lived `debian:bookworm` container that mounts `$(DOCKER_ROOT)` and removes its contents from inside the container.
